title: Fix Yarn 1 next tag lookups
body:
Related to #36129

## Failure observed

This failed during downstream upgrade verification for #36129. The component-subtitle migration itself completed, but its production-built Storybook CLI then updated the Box UI Elements fixture through the local Verdaccio registry.

At that dependency-update step, the CLI wrote these literal ranges to the fixture's `package.json`:

- `@chromatic-com/storybook: ^next`
- `@storybook/addon-webpack5-compiler-babel: ^next`

Yarn 1.22.22 failed on the next `yarn install` because `^next` is a dist-tag name, not a resolvable semver range. The installed Storybook 10.5.0 baseline had passed its build/runtime check before the upgrade. This PR fixes the shared Yarn 1 lookup that generated those ranges; it does not change the subtitle migration.

## What I did

Fixed Yarn 1 package metadata lookup for satellite addon upgrades.

- Read dist-tags for `@next` requests and return the concrete next version.
- Return `null` when a package has no next tag, so the upgrade omits it instead of writing an invalid `^next` range.
- Added regression coverage for both paths.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [ ] stories
- [x] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

No manual browser QA is needed. The focused unit regression covers tag resolution and the missing-tag case. The dependency path was also verified with Yarn 1.22.22 in Box UI Elements at `2dd680d225f0b4b762c00f84cc171eb6b6fd2a2f`: after changing `@chromatic-com/storybook` from `^5.2.1` to `^5.4.0-next.1`, `yarn install --ignore-scripts --non-interactive` completed successfully. `@storybook/addon-webpack5-compiler-babel` remained `^4.0.1` because it has no next dist-tag.
